title: HLS Runtime Lifecycle Boundary
problem: HLS session lifecycle, admission, readiness, segment waits, and cleanup are distributed across server playback composition, HLS app service, artifact service, transcode runner, and startup cleanup, which will make queueing, artifact I/O pressure, remote workers, and LL-HLS harder to add safely.
gates: git diff --check -- docs/workstreams/hls-runtime-lifecycle-boundary docs/architecture/PLAYBACK.md docs/architecture/LANES.md docs/architecture/WORKSTREAM_LINKS.md docs/workstreams/README.md

evidence.summary: Froze current HLS lifecycle invariants, cleanup ownership, readiness and one-shot segment wait semantics, test coverage map, and the decision to split artifact I/O pressure into a PAIP follow-on without changing Rust behavior.

Added behavior-preserving HLS lifecycle tests for timeout cleanup, HLS stale startup recovery, and remote staged-input release across success, runner error, and admission rejection. Planner accepted a narrow Admin DTO stage mapping fix for HardwarePipelineStage::ToneMap and SubtitleBurnIn. Final HLS, fmt, and diff gates passed; one progressive-readiness test remains load-sensitive under full-suite concurrency.

Split follow-ons: make HLS progressive-readiness test stability the recommended next bounded playback-transcode workstream, keep PAIP artifact I/O pressure as a playback/storage follow-on, keep resource admission unification, remote workers, LL-HLS/CMAF, and player UX as separate proposed lanes.

continue_policy.notes: Continue with HRLB-040 closeout. Verify final gates, preserve the HRLB-030 follow-on decisions, and close or split remaining work. Recommended next workstream after closeout: proposed:hls-progressive-readiness-test-stability. Do not implement PAIP artifact I/O pressure enforcement, resource admission unification, remote workers, LL-HLS/CMAF, or player UX until the planner opens dedicated workstreams.
